spec_match.rationale: The shared-edge motivation and the column-rule/row-rule-in-gap CSS are spec-accurate, but the support probe checks CSS.supports('column-rule','1px solid black') — a multicol property true in every browser — so the pill reports 'yes' here while the gap-rule grid renders no lines at all (classic false support probe).

interactive.rationale: There are no controls whatsoever — two static grids, a static zoom probe and static code blocks; invariant 7's minimum for CSS features is a toggle/slider/before-after that changes rendered output on interaction.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises exactly this static side-by-side, zoomed probe and code comparison.

edge_cases.rationale: There is a declared fallback path (grey gap background when unsupported), but it never activates because the probe can't return false, so unsupported browsers see the 'yes' pill over an empty-gap grid.

references.rationale: The ChromeStatus link points at feature 5202274007539712, not this folder's identity 5157805733183488 — a wrong-id reference that would mislead the slug self-heal script.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite probes the real gap-decoration surface (row-rule longhands, rule shorthands, CSSOM round-trip) and honestly fails 6 of 8 in this browser — notably contradicting the page's own pill.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): border grid shows doubled edges correctly, gap-rule grid shows no rules, pill falsely reads yes, and the right-hand code block visibly overflows the page edge at 1280px. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

design_system.rationale: Colours are variables and the mode-button pattern sets background+color, but the code-pair grid lets a <pre> blow out its 1fr track, producing horizontal overflow on desktop (and worse on mobile).

accessibility.rationale: Content is mostly static text with proper headings, but the support pill state is colour+text with no live region, and the visual double-line vs single-line distinction has no textual equivalent beyond the probe notes.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The second code block overflows the viewport horizontally even at 1280px desktop (screenshot evidence); .code-block has no overflow-x handling and grid children no min-width:0, so a ≈360px viewport will scroll horizontally.

openQuestions.title: Fix the false support probe — test the gap-decoration surface, not multicol column-rule
openQuestions.detail: CSS.supports('column-rule','1px solid black') has been true since multicol shipped, so the pill claims support everywhere and the grey-gap fallback never activates; this session showed 'column-rule on grid: yes' above a gap-rule grid with zero rules while the conformance suite failed 6/8. Probe the real contract instead — CSS.supports('row-rule-color','red') or the rule shorthand (the suite's own assertions) — so the pill and fallback behave honestly.

openQuestions.title: Correct the ChromeStatus reference to feature 5157805733183488
openQuestions.detail: The see-also links chromestatus.com/feature/5202274007539712, but every other page in this folder (and the feature index) uses 5157805733183488. The embedded id is the self-heal anchor, so a wrong id is actively harmful.

openQuestions.title: Contain the code-pair overflow
openQuestions.detail: The right code block escapes the page's right edge at 1280px because the <pre> content forces its 1fr grid track wide (min-width:auto blowout). Add min-width:0 to .code-block and overflow-x:auto to its pre; re-check at ≈360px where the page currently scrolls horizontally.

openQuestions.title: Add the minimum interaction invariant 7 requires
openQuestions.detail: A toggle that switches one grid between the border approach and the gap-rule approach (or a rule-width slider shared by both panels) would turn this from a static card pair into the required hands-on comparison, and would make the zoom probe's 4px-vs-2px claim observable by the user.

openQuestions.title: Announce probe state non-visually
openQuestions.detail: Give the support pill role=status or aria-live so the detected state is perceivable, and add a sentence of text equivalent describing the visual difference between the two panels when rules are supported.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-gap-decorations/border-vs-rule-compare/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 6 fail / 0 blocked). The border panel correctly shows doubled shared edges, but the page's own probe is false-positive (multicol column-rule), the gap-rule panel renders lineless with a green 'yes' pill above it, the ChromeStatus id is wrong, the page has no interactive control at all, and the code comparison overflows the viewport on desktop. No interactions existed to drive headless.
